title: Stars and the Stellar Lifecycle
text: Stars form from collapsing clouds of gas and dust and spend most of their lives fusing hydrogen into helium in their cores (the main-sequence stage). A star's eventual fate depends on its mass: low-mass stars like the Sun expand into red giants and shed their outer layers, leaving a white dwarf; massive stars can explode as supernovae, leaving behind a neutron star or black hole.
